answer: Require each agent to earn a nontransferable reputation through repeated, costly participation: for example, completing small escrowed tasks whose results are checked by randomly selected peers, with disputes forfeiting the deposit. A karst-like network of trust links can give newcomers a narrow terrace of limited access until they build a verified thread of successful work. One attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each deposit and sustain each identity’s history, making mass Sybils expensive rather than merely a matter of minting accounts.
